content: 1. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of oliceridine by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. If coadministration with a CYP3A4 inducer is necessary, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable drug effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the oliceridine dosage and monitor for respiratory depression. 2. Rifampin decreases omeprazole levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Rifampin reduces ondansetron levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Rifampin decreases osilodrostat levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Osilodrostat is a substrate of CYP3A4 and CYP2B6. Monitor for changes in drug efficacy or adverse effects during coadministration or discontinuation with strong CYP3A4 and/or CYP2B6 inducers. 5. Rifampin reduces ospemifene levels by inducing metabolism through hepatic enzymes CYP3A4, CYP2C19, and CYP2C9/10. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Rifampin decreases oxybutynin levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Rifampin reduces oxycodone levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Rifampin decreases paclitaxel levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, and other mechanisms. Paclitaxel efficacy may also decrease when coadministered with CYP2C8 inducers. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Rifampin reduces paliperidone levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Paliperidone dosage may need to be increased when coadministered with strong inducers of both CYP3A4 and P-gp. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 10. Rifampin decreases pantoprazole levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Rifampin reduces parecoxib levels or effects by inducing metabolism through hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Rifampin decreases paromomycin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Rifampin reduces pentobarbital levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Rifampin decreases phenobarbital levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Rifampin reduces phenytoin levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Rifampin decreases pimavanserin levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration if possible. Monitor for reduced pimavanserin efficacy, and consider increasing the dosage if necessary. 17. Rifampin reduces pimozide levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Rifampin decreases pioglitazone levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Rifampin increases pitavastatin levels by decreasing metabolism. Do not exceed 2 mg/day of pitavastatin. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Rifampin reduces pitolisant levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Pitolisant exposure decreases by 50% when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. If the inducer is discontinued, reduce the pitolisant dosage by half. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 21. Rifampin decreases polatuzumab vedotin levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Polatuzumab undergoes catabolism to small peptides, amino acids, monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE), and unconjugated MMAE-related catabolites. MMAE is a CYP3A4 substrate. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inducer may decrease unconjugated MMAE AUC. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Ponatinib increases rifampin levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Rifampin reduces posaconazole levels or effects by inducing metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Rifampin increases pravastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Rifampin decreases prednisolone levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Rifampin reduces prednisone levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Pretomanid increases rifampin levels or effects through unspecified mechanisms. Monitor for drug-related adverse effects if pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Rifampin decreases primidone levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Probenecid increases rifampin levels or effects through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Concomitant use may increase rifampin concentration and toxicity risk. Monitor for adverse reactions during coadministration. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Rifampin reduces propafenone levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Rifampin decreases propranolol levels by increasing metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Rifampin reduces quinine levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Rifampin decreases rabeprazole levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Rifampin reduces raltegravir levels by increasing hepatic clearance. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Rifampin decreases ramelteon levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzymes CYP1A2 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Rifampin reduces rasagiline levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Rifampin is a relatively weak CYP1A2 inducer; caution is advised. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Rifampin decreases riociguat levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Data for dose adjustment is not available. 38. Rifampin reduces risperidone levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Rifampin decreases ritonavir levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Rifampin reduces rivaroxaban levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid concomitant use with drugs that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers. If coadministration is necessary, consider increasing the rivaroxaban dose. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Rifampin decreases romidepsin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Rifampin reduces ropinirole levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Rifampin increases rosuvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Rifampin decreases ruxolitinib levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Rifampin reduces ruxolitinib topical levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Rifampin increases sacubitril/valsartan levels or effects through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition. Coadministration with OATP1B1 inhibitors may increase valsartan systemic exposure. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Sarecycline increases rifampin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor for toxicities of P-gp substrates that may require dosage reduction when coadministered with P-gp inhibitors. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Rifampin reduces saxagliptin levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Rifampin decreases seladelpar levels or effects by increasing metabolism. Monitor biochemical response (e.g., ALP and bilirubin) when initiating rifampin during seladelpar treatment. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Rifampin reduces selegiline levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 51. Rifampin decreases selexipag levels or effects by inducing metabolism through CYP2C8, UGT1A3, and UGT2B7 enzymes. Coadministration decreases exposure to selexipag's active metabolite by 50%. Increase the selexipag dose up to twice the typical dose if coadministered with rifampin. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Rifampin reduces sildenafil levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Potent CYP3A4 inducers are expected to cause substantial decreases in sildenafil plasma levels. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Rifampin decreases silodosin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Rifampin increases simvastatin toxicity through mechanisms involving OATP1B1 inhibition, which may increase the risk of myopathy. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Rifampin reduces sirolimus levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Sodium bicarbonate decreases rifampin levels or effects through mechanisms involving reduced absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before ingestion of antacids. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Rifampin decreases the effects of sodium picosulfate/magnesium oxide/anhydrous citric acid by altering metabolism. Coadministration with antibiotics decreases efficacy by altering colonic bacterial flora needed to convert sodium picosulfate to its active form. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Magnesium sulfate/potassium chloride increases rifampin toxicity through mechanisms involving fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Sodium sulfate/potassium sulfate/magnesium sulfate increases rifampin toxicity through mechanisms involving fluid and electrolyte abnormalities, which may increase the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Sparsentan decreases rifampin levels or effects by inducing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Sparsentan, a CYP2B6 inducer, reduces the efficacy of CYP2B6 substrates. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Stiripentol increases rifampin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Stiripentol is both a CYP2B6 inhibitor and inducer. Monitor CYP2B6 substrates coadministered with stiripentol for increased or decreased effects. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Rifampin reduces streptomycin levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 63. Rifampin decreases sufentanil levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inducers may decrease sufentanil levels and efficacy, potentially precipitating withdrawal syndrome in patients with physical dependence. Discontinuation of CYP3A4 inducers may increase sufentanil plasma concentration. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 64. Sulopenem etzadroxil/probenecid increases rifampin levels by decreasing metabolism. Probenecid, an OAT1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of drugs dependent on OAT1/3 for elimination. Monitor more frequently for adverse reactions associated with rifampin. Use caution and monitor closely. 65. Rifampin reduces suvorexant levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Strong CYP3A4 inducers may decrease suvorexant efficacy. If an increased dose is required, do not exceed 20 mg/day. Use caution and monitor closely. 66. Rifampin decreases tacrolimus levels or effects via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 67. Rifampin reduces tadalafil levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid combination in pulmonary hypertension patients. For patients with erectile dysfunction, monitor response to tadalafil carefully due to potential for decreased effectiveness. Use caution and monitor closely. 68. Rifampin decreases tamoxifen levels or effects by inducing metabolism through hepatic enzymes CYP2C9/10 and CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 69. Rifampin reduces tasimelteon levels or effects by inducing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inducers. Use caution and monitor closely.
